identity.real_world_identity_notes: The submitted RaceRoom identity maps to Porsche's factory 944 Turbo Cup one-make race-car series, launched in 1986 and replaced by the Carrera Cup in 1990. The series identity spans multiple seasons and year-specific specifications; the simulator name does not identify a single chassis or season. Porsche's own history places the Turbo Cup at the start of its one-make series in 1986 and records the 1990 transition to Carrera Cup. An exact 1986 Turbo Cup auction catalogue records five forward gears and a manual transmission, while period Turbo Cup specifications and the 944 Turbo workshop manual corroborate the five-speed manual platform, clutch pedal, and synchromesh construction. The repository contains no existing curated Porsche 944 Turbo Cup record, so this is a create-new proposal.

claims.basis: Porsche's own history places the Turbo Cup at the start of its one-make series in 1986 and records the 1990 transition to Carrera Cup. An exact 1986 Turbo Cup auction catalogue records five forward gears and a manual transmission, while period Turbo Cup specifications and the 944 Turbo workshop manual corroborate the five-speed manual platform, clutch pedal, and synchromesh construction. The repository contains no existing curated Porsche 944 Turbo Cup record, so this is a create-new proposal.

The exact 1986 Turbo Cup catalogue explicitly records five forward gears, and the 944 Turbo workshop manual and 1988 Turbo Cup specification corroborate the five-speed manual platform. The 944 Turbo workshop manual documents the 016 R/S five-speed manual transmission and synchromesh rings, while Turbo Cup-specific sources describe strengthened gears rather than a dog-ring conversion. This supports a medium-confidence synchromesh classification for the Cup's 944 Turbo transmission basis, with the exact year-specific race preparation still a review caveat. The exact Turbo Cup is documented with a manual transmission, and the period material describes a gear lever and shifting through the gate. The reviewed evidence supports a driver-operated H-pattern lever, although no chassis-specific full gate photograph was decisive. The period driving material describes the five-speed gear lever moving through a conventional gate, and the workshop material documents the manual 944 Turbo selector. No source reviewed shows a dogleg or sequential selector; the exact gate layout should remain a review point rather than being read from the simulator cockpit. The 944 Turbo platform has a physical clutch pedal and the Turbo Cup received a heavy-duty racing clutch. With a driver-operated H-pattern manual transmission, the clutch is required to pull away from rest; this is a mechanism-based derivation, not a simulator observation. The documented synchromesh construction maps to a required clutch technique for the authentic running upshift under the data model, and the platform has a physical clutch pedal. The claim is derived from mechanism, not from the RaceRoom drive. The documented synchromesh construction maps to a required clutch technique for the authentic running downshift under the data model. No simulator behavior is used to establish this real-car value. The synchromesh construction matches the documented derivation: a manual rev-match blip can ease the synchronizers but is not required for the gear to engage. This is an authentic technique classification, not evidence that every driver used it on every downshift. A rev-match blip is a downshift technique for this synchromesh manual gearbox; the reviewed sources establish no separate upshift blip action. The reviewed manual gearbox sources establish no automatic rev-match action for an upshift; automatic blip is a downshift concept here. The reviewed sources establish downshift rev matching as the relevant optional technique but do not prescribe a separate downshift throttle-lift step. The reviewed manual and Turbo Cup modification sources establish a mechanically operated manual gearbox, not a downshift torque-cut procedure; no separate automatic cut is established for downshift. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shape, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/integrated_display, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/open_top.
